References: Image 1 is THE REFERENCE INSTALLATION: recreate this space, its layout, camera height, light and mood; but every screen, lightbox, cube face or projection in it becomes a plain white glowing surface with nothing on it, no images, faces, text or colour. The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera at standing height, straight on, 35mm lens, f/4. The wall panel sits on the centre line, filling about 60 percent of the frame width, its face square to the camera; its light makes a long soft reflection on the polished floor below; a low ceiling with a warm wood soffit crosses the top of the frame; dark glass doors at one side. One visitor walks past at the right edge, small. Visitors appear only as small dark silhouettes, seen from behind against the light, never more than a fraction of the frame; no face or profile shows.

Place: A large contemporary art museum after dark: polished dark stone or concrete floors that reflect the light, dark walls, a dark ceiling; the installation is the only light in the room.

Light: The installation's own glow is the only light: it spills onto the polished floor in long reflections and onto the people near it, then falls off into deep shadow. No other lamps.

Palette and grade: Neutral: soft blacks, charcoal, warm grey stone, natural skin; the glowing surfaces are pure neutral white. No green, teal, blue or orange cast. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of an art installation, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, the way an exhibition photographer frames the work, never a tiny object in a big room. It is a real photograph made in camera by an art documentation photographer, not a render. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The space shows small honest signs of use; the design surface itself is new and clean. The glowing surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation, bloom, haze or glow over it.

Design surface: THE WALL PANEL FACE IS PLAIN EVENLY LIT WHITE, glowing bright and clean edge to edge, clearly the brightest thing in the frame yet not blown out, with crisp corners; nothing on it.

Finish: Shot on a full-frame camera at ISO 1600 by a professional exhibition photographer: honest dark exposure, fine natural grain, true neutral colour, crisp lines, gentle lens falloff. Quiet, expensive and real, like the press image of a major museum show; never a render.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, any image, photo, face, text or colour on any screen or lightbox, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, a green or teal cast, any object not named in the shot, fog or haze, a clean smooth digital look.
